beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:setting the scene, quiet wonder]^Thousands of inscriptions from one of the world's first great ^civilisations, along the ^Indus river. [act:hushed, the hook lands]And ^nobody alive can read@present them.
[d:tension][act:a sly aside, eyebrows up][tune:risefall]There's now a ^million-dollar prize for whoever ^can.

[d:calm][p:0.93][act:setting the scene, unhurried]The Indus valley, in today's ^Pakistan and western ^India, about {2600|twenty-six hundred} to {1900|nineteen hundred} BCE, some four to four and a half thousand years ago. [act:quietly impressed]Planned cities, with ^drains. [go:2|0][act:leaning in, curious]And their ^writing, mostly on tiny seals the size of a postage ^stamp. [p:0.9][act:the everyday picture, wry]About ^five signs each: shorter than a text ^message.

[d:build][p:0.93][act:explaining, even-handed]Most experts say it ^is writing: some signs stand for ^words, others for ^sounds, read@past right to left. [p:0.9][act:the everyday picture, playful]Like a picture puzzle, where a bee and a leaf spell ^belief.

[d:build][sfx:shimmer][act:the counter-claim, intrigued]But in {2004|two thousand four} three scholars argued it might not be ^language at all: the texts are so ^short, and signs so rarely ^repeat inside one. [act:offering it plainly][tune:level]Perhaps ^emblems, then. [act:a modern comparison, lighter][tune:fall]Like ^logos: meaningful, but not spelling out ^words.

[d:build][act:warm, a little conspiratorial]And it has ^company. [act:counting them off][tune:level]^Linear A, on clay tablets from ^Crete. [act:next one, same rhythm][tune:level]^Rongorongo, on wooden boards from Easter ^Island. [act:the last one, landing it][tune:fall]And the ^Phaistos disc, also from Crete: one of a ^kind.

[d:aside][p:0.93][act:lighter, half-smiling]Some of these we can ^sound out... [act:the gentle sting]and still not understand a ^word. [p:0.9][act:the everyday picture, warm]Like reading aloud in a language you never ^learned.

[d:reveal][act:brightening, hopeful]But scripts ^do fall. [act:plain fact, a nod]Linear ^B, a cousin of Linear A, in {1952|nineteen fifty-two}. [sfx:hit][act:wonder, savouring it]And in {2022|twenty twenty-two}, Linear ^Elamite, from Iran, cracked with royal names on ^silver cups. [p:0.93][act:the method, explaining]A king's name sounds much the same in ^any language, so it gives away the sounds of its ^signs. [p:0.9][act:the everyday picture, playful]Like a ^crossword: the answers you know unlock the ^rest.
[d:build][go:4|0][act:bright, raising the stakes]Now the government of ^Tamil Nadu, a state in southern India, offers a million dollars for cracking the ^Indus script.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm][tune:rise]The Indus signs write a ^language? [act:the verdict, measured][tune:fall]^*Plausible*. [act:fair, even]Most experts lean ^yes. [act:honest, a touch lower][tune:fall]Nobody has ^shown it yet.

[d:tension][p:0.93][act:explaining, gentle]A bilingual: the same message in two scripts, one of them readable, like a sign at an ^airport. [p:0.9][act:quiet, the wish]What's missing is one ^long text, or one ^bilingual.
